items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: My playing had been strongly influenced by Fats Waller and Earl Hines

ctx.x: Yeah. Which started out to be actually what I always think of as the most important era of my particular musical career. Nevertheless, before I get into that, I would like to go back and talk about some other things. Because when you are talking about your career or your life or something like that, it's impossible, I think, to just go in a straight chronological line and bring out everything that happened. Because while one thing is happening, something else is happening at the same time. So right now, I'd like…

I think it was around 1936... My playing had been strongly influenced by Fats Waller and Earl Hines, and somewhere between there I was trying to find a good way to play the piano. As far as a style was concerned, I hadn't thought so much about that; I was always more or less copying everything I heard.
